author: Ozanne-Rivierre, Françoise
title: The Proto-Oceanic consonantal system and the languages of New Caledonia
notes: Consulted directly on 23 November 2026 (JSTOR PDF; tables and examples read from page images): the POc system she assumes (Table 1, p. 192), reflexes of POc *t, *d, *s, *k in the northern languages (Table 2, p. 194), POc *q (pp. 194-196), the prenasalised series (pp. 196-201; Table 3, Drubea, p. 199), and the PNC consonant system with its innovations from POc (Table 4 and §5, p. 202; notes 5, 9-12, pp. 204-205). Her POc *d is Ross's *r and her *nt, *nd are Ross's *d, *dr (p. 196).

author: Geraghty, Paul
title: The reconstruction of Proto-Southern Oceanic
notes: Consulted directly on 23 November 2026 (scan with a cropped left margin, ABBYY text layer): orthography (Table 1, p. 143), innovations shared with Vanuatu (pp. 148-150) and the phonological innovations of PSO (pp. 150-151). Geraghty's Southern Oceanic is New Caledonia and the Loyalty Islands (p. 141), the Proto-New Caledonian node here, not the Southern Oceanic of Lynch and Ross, which includes Vanuatu. He derives PSO from his Proto-Eastern Oceanic.
